stories.research_notes:
Here’s a factual research note on the report “Burned area in conservation units drops 68.79% in Minas Gerais”:

---

## What the sources say

### Primary Source
- The data comes from a **partial (i.e. not year-end) official assessment by the Corpo de Bombeiros Militar de Minas Gerais (CBMMG)**, coordinated with the Força-Tarefa Previncêndio (FTP) and Agência Minas (the state’s press agency). ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))

### Key Figures & Findings
- As of *November 2026*, about **16,680 hectares** of state conservation units had been burned. ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))
- This represents a **68.79% reduction** compared to the historical annual average used by CBMMG. ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))
- Compared with the average for 2024–2025, the reduction is **55.45%** (historical mean of 37,440 hectares vs 16,680 hectares) ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))
- Also, **84% of fires** in 2026 were extinguished within the first 24 hours, up from about 70.2% in 2025. ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))
- Approximately **99.57%** of the territory of the conservation units had **no recorded burn damage** as of that report date. ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))

### Context & Initiatives
- CBMMG has led the coordination of conservation units’ fire prevention and response since **2024**, through FTP. ([jornaldeuberaba.com.br](https://www.jornaldeuberaba.com.br/noticia/170596/balanco-2023-2026-area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-gerais-cai-68-79-em-relacao-a-media-historica?utm_source=openai))
- Measures cited: implementation of **bases operacionais avançadas** (advanced operational bases), specialized military staff, improved management of contracted brigadistas (fire brigades). ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))
- Use of **GeoFOGO**, a satellite-based platform (using ArcGIS), implemented in 2025 and improved in 2026, for monitoring burned areas. ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))
- Staffing includes roughly **280 brigadistas** across **40 conservation units** in 2026, compared to 36 units in earlier years. Also **8 advanced bases** supporting operations. ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))

---

## Distinguishing Completed/Measured Outcomes vs Plans

What is confirmed (measured outcome):
- The reported **reductions in burned area** (68.79% vs historical average; 55.45% vs 2024-25) are actual measured data as of November 2026. ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))
- The proportion of fires extinguished within 24 hours (84%) is a measured operational outcome. ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))
- The coverage figure of conservation unit territories remaining unburned (99.57%) is also a measured statistic. ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))

What is planning or pending:
- The historical average period is unspecified in reports—not clear which years are used for the “historical annual average”. ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))
- Data is partial (not covering full year 2026), and the fire season or “estação de incêndios” is still ongoing. So final annual totals may differ. ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))
- Future plans mentioned include expanding GeoFOGO’s licenses and features, developing a wildfire-risk alert system, building more advanced bases, and training volunteer brigadistas in 2027. These are announced intentions rather than completed. ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))

---

## Assessment of Multiple Reports & Repetition

- The data has been widely reported across state media, local news sites, and emergency or environmental reporting outlets, all citing CBMMG and Agência Minas. Many articles appear to draw from the same press release or official briefing. ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))
- The published numbers are consistent across the independent sources (e.g. Mais Minas, Portal Impactto, Estado de Minas). ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))

---

## Remaining Open Questions & Data Gaps

- What is the exact range of years used to calculate the “historical annual average” that serves as baseline for the 68.79% drop. Reports do not specify. ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))
- How much variation exists across different conservation units or biomes (e.g. Cerrado vs Atlantic Forest) in the state.
- Whether federal conservation units are included, or just state units.
- What the climate/weather contributions are (rainfall, drought, El Niño) versus operational improvements. Some sources mention favorable rainfall and climatic conditions may have helped. ([ief.mg.gov.br](https://www.ief.mg.gov.br/w/minas-gerais-registra-redu%C3%A7%C3%A3o-de-44-nos-focos-de-calor-em-2026-nas-unidades-de-conserva%C3%A7%C3%A3o?p_l_back_url=%2Fweb%2Fief%2Fnoticias%3FassetCategoryIds%3D8330774%26delta%3D8%26start%3D2&p_l_back_url_title=Noticias&utm_source=openai))

---

## Summary

- As of **November 2026**, state conservation units in Minas Gerais suffered **≈ 16,680 hectares** of burning, which is **68.79% below** the state’s historical annual average for burned area. This is a measured outcome. ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))
- Compared to just the previous two years (2024–2025), the burned area dropped by about **55.45%**. ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))
- Fire suppression timeliness has improved: **84%** of fire events are extinguished within the first 24 hours in 2026 (vs ~70.2% in 2025). ([maisminas.com.br](https://maisminas.com.br/noticias-mg/area-queimada-em-unidades-de-conservacao-de-minas-em-2026-fica-6879-abaixo-da-media-historica/?utm_source=openai))
- However, data are still partial (the season is ongoing), and baseline period for “historical average” is not clearly defined. The figures also rely heavily on CBMMG’s assessment via FTP, so some dependence on agency reporting.

---

If you like, I can try to find the underlying CBMMG or government published report (PDF) to verify the baseline years and get more granular data by UC or biome.

stories.research_notes:
Here’s a research-note on what actually happened with the “Tunnels to Towers Foundation opens veterans housing community in Harrisburg” story, based on primary and independent sources:

---

## What Happened

- On **November 11, 2026** (Veterans Day), the Tunnel to Towers Foundation officially opened the **Harrisburg Veterans Village**, a housing community for veterans in need of permanent supportive housing. ([t2t.org](https://t2t.org/tunnel-to-towers-foundation-commemorates-veterans-day-with-30-mortgage-payoffs-and-grand-opening-of-veterans-village/?utm_source=openai))  
- The facility was built on the site of the former Phoenix Steel Mill in South Harrisburg, on S. Front Street, near the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation building. ([theburgnews.com](https://theburgnews.com/news/village-providing-housing-for-homeless-veterans-cuts-the-ribbon-in-harrisburg?utm_source=openai))

---

## Key Details & Outcomes

- The Village includes a **64-unit apartment building** plus **20 one-bedroom “comfort homes”**, totaling 84 units. These provide housing for more than **80 veterans**. ([t2t.org](https://t2t.org/the-tunnel-to-towers-foundation-to-break-ground-on-veterans-village-in-harrisburg/?utm_source=openai))  
- On-site services will be provided, including job training, benefits assistance, mental health support, addiction treatment, case management, financial coaching, and other therapeutic services. ([t2t.org](https://t2t.org/the-tunnel-to-towers-foundation-to-break-ground-on-veterans-village-in-harrisburg/?utm_source=openai))  
- The development is a $20-million project (as reported by *TheBurg*) and was under construction after breaking ground in **April 2025**. ([theburgnews.com](https://theburgnews.com/news/village-providing-housing-for-homeless-veterans-cuts-the-ribbon-in-harrisburg?utm_source=openai))  
- Residents will be charged a program fee that covers both housing and support services—approximately **$900/month** for the apartments and **$950/month** for the comfort homes. ([theburgnews.com](https://theburgnews.com/news/harrisburg-housing-for-homeless-veterans-nears-completion-preps-for-ribbon-cutting?utm_source=openai))  
- Lease-up: About one quarter of the units were pre-leased by the time of ribbon-cutting. The remainder expected to be leased by **mid-2027**. ([theburgnews.com](https://theburgnews.com/news/village-providing-housing-for-homeless-veterans-cuts-the-ribbon-in-harrisburg?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Source Assessment

- **Primary source**: Tunnel to Towers Foundation itself published a press release confirming:
  - the grand opening date (Nov 11, 2026),  
  - size of project,  
  - number/types of units,  
  - supportive services to be offered. ([t2t.org](https://t2t.org/tunnel-to-towers-foundation-commemorates-veterans-day-with-30-mortgage-payoffs-and-grand-opening-of-veterans-village/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Independent/local coverage**: *TheBurg* offered detailed reporting including cost, location, fee structure for residents, pre-leasing/lease-up schedule, construction timeline and local context (Phoenix Steel Mill site, riverfront, etc.). ([theburgnews.com](https://theburgnews.com/news/village-providing-housing-for-homeless-veterans-cuts-the-ribbon-in-harrisburg?utm_source=openai))  

---

## What Is a Plan/Pledge vs. a Measured Outcome

| Item | Completion Status |
|---|---|
| Grand opening of Veterans Village | **Completed** on Nov 11, 2026. ([t2t.org](https://t2t.org/tunnel-to-towers-foundation-commemorates-veterans-day-with-30-mortgage-payoffs-and-grand-opening-of-veterans-village/?utm_source=openai)) |
| Construction of the 84 units (64 apartments + 20 comfort homes) | **Completed** as part of opening. ([t2t.org](https://t2t.org/tunnel-to-towers-foundation-commemorates-veterans-day-with-30-mortgage-payoffs-and-grand-opening-of-veterans-village/?utm_source=openai)) |
| On-site services established | Declared as part of the facility at opening; implies operations are in place. ([t2t.org](https://t2t.org/tunnel-to-towers-foundation-commemorates-veterans-day-with-30-mortgage-payoffs-and-grand-opening-of-veterans-village/?utm_source=openai)) |
| Resident move-in and leasing | Initially pre-leasing (≈25 %) at opening; full leasing expected by mid-2027. ([theburgnews.com](https://theburgnews.com/news/village-providing-housing-for-homeless-veterans-cuts-the-ribbon-in-harrisburg?utm_source=openai)) |
| Program fees charged to residents | Established as operational detail (rent + services fee) from early-opening phase. ([theburgnews.com](https://theburgnews.com/news/harrisburg-housing-for-homeless-veterans-nears-completion-preps-for-ribbon-cutting?utm_source=openai)) |

---

If you like, I can also track how many veterans have moved in so far, or what the local response has been since opening.

Here’s a researched fact-note on the event “India’s renewable energy expansion averts $100 bn in fuel imports” based primarily on the original source (IEA report) and independent reporting. --- ## What actually happened - The International Energy Agency (IEA) released its *India Renewable Energy Market Report 2026* on **November 3, 2026**. ([iea.org](https://www.iea.org/news/indias-rapid-renewables-growth-is-strengthening-its-role-in-global-energy-markets-iea-report-finds?utm_source=openai)) - That report finds that India’s growth in solar photovoltaic (PV), wind, and bioenergy capacity since 2010 has enabled it to **avoid more than USD 100 billion** in coal and natural gas import costs between **2011 and 2025**. ([iea.org](https://www.iea.org/news/indias-rapid-renewables-growth-is-strengthening-its-role-in-global-energy-markets-iea-report-finds?utm_source=openai)) - It projects that cumulative savings could rise to nearly **USD 240 billion** by **2030** (assuming fuel prices stay around their 2024-25 average). ([business-standard.com](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/industry/news/india-s-renewable-energy-push-saved-100-bn-in-fuel-imports-iea-report-126111101361_1.html?isa=yes&utm_source=openai)) --- ## Supporting details from the report - Without the solar, wind, and bioenergy capacity added since 2010, India would have had to import about **110 million tonnes more coal in 2025 alone**. ([iea.org](https://www.iea.org/news/indias-rapid-renewables-growth-is-strengthening-its-role-in-global-energy-markets-iea-report-finds?utm_source=openai)) - India’s installed renewable power capacity has almost **quadrupled over the past decade**, exceeding **300 GW** in 2026. ([iea.org](https://www.iea.org/news/indias-rapid-renewables-growth-is-strengthening-its-role-in-global-energy-markets-iea-report-finds?utm_source=openai)) - The country achieved the target of **50 % of installed electricity capacity from non-fossil sources** in 2025—five years ahead of its 2030 goal. ([iea.org](https://www.iea.org/news/indias-rapid-renewables-growth-is-strengthening-its-role-in-global-energy-markets-iea-report-finds?utm_source=openai)) --- ## What is established vs. what is projected | Type | Content | |---|---| | **Measured / completed outcomes** | • Avoided USD 100 billion in fossil fuel imports (coal + natural gas) over 2011–2025 due to renewable energy deployment.
• Avoided importing ~110 million tonnes of coal in 2025 alone compared to a counterfactual scenario with no new solar, wind, bioenergy since 2010.
• Non-fossil installed power capacity hit 50 % in 2025.
• India’s renewable installed capacity appears to be over 300 GW as of 2026. | | **Projections / upcoming estimates** | • Savings could grow to ~USD 240 billion by 2030 (assuming 2024-25 fuel price levels).
• Annual savings could be ~USD 35 billion by 2030.
• Forecasts of capacity rising to ~530 GW by 2030, with solar PV accounting for over 80 % of new additions.
• Renewables supplying ~35 % of India’s electricity by 2030. | --- ## Original / primary source - The IEA’s *India Renewable Energy Market Report 2026* is the primary source for these findings. ([iea.org](https://www.iea.org/files/9452aeba-6c64-4dfa-9205-569c354b686e/IndiaRenewableEnergyMarketReport2026.pdf?utm_source=openai)) - In particular, Chapter 3 in the report contains a scenario-analysis showing what India’s fuel import bills and coal import volumes would have been under a “low renewables” counterfactual in which no new non-hydro renewables were added after 2010. ([iea.org](https://www.iea.org/files/9452aeba-6c64-4dfa-9205-569c354b686e/IndiaRenewableEnergyMarketReport2026.pdf?utm_source=openai)) --- ## Independent confirmation - Multiple Indian news outlets (The Economic Times, Business Standard, Tribune India, etc.) have reported on the IEA’s findings, quoting the USD 100 billion avoided import cost, the USD 240 billion projected savings by 2030, and the avoided 110 million tonnes of coal in 2025. ([economictimes.indiatimes.com](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/renewables/indias-renewable-energy-expansion-averts-100-bn-in-fuel-imports-savings-seen-at-240-bn-by-2030/articleshow/135739839.cms?from=mdr&utm_source=openai)) - These reports draw directly from IEA’s report or accompanying press releases. There is no evidence that any independent research outside the IEA has recalculated and confirmed these numbers as of yet. --- If you like, I can also pull up responses from experts analyzing the methodology—strengths, limitations—to understand how robust these estimates are.

**Research note — November 11, 2026**

- Bioengineer.org’s article describes a **scoping review**, not a newly implemented water-access intervention. It reports that the review covered 30 studies across 17 countries and found associations between water access and lower risk of some skin neglected tropical diseases. It gives an adjusted odds ratio of 0.2 for water access and Buruli ulcer. The article says most of the evidence was observational, so this does **not** establish that improved water access caused a measured reduction in disease. ([bioengineer.org](https://bioengineer.org/improved-water-access-and-environmental-management-associated-with-lower-skin-ntd-risk/?utm_source=openai))
- Bioengineer.org credits **Scienmag** as the news source; Scienmag carries substantially the same article and claims the review appeared in *PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases* as article e0014392. These are not independent confirmations of the findings. ([bioengineer.org](https://bioengineer.org/improved-water-access-and-environmental-management-associated-with-lower-skin-ntd-risk/?utm_source=openai))
- **Verification limitation:** I could not locate the cited primary paper in the searches conducted, so its publication details and reported results remain unverified here. No independent report confirming this specific study was found.
- **Bottom line:** The candidate’s wording risks implying a proven health improvement. The available news copy describes reported associations in prior research—not a completed intervention or demonstrated causal reduction in NTD risk.

stories.research_notes:
Here is what I found, based on the primary source and independent reports, about the claim: *“Luoma Lake Fishing Ban Spurs Fish Biomass Recovery”*.

---

## What Actually Happened

### Primary Source: Peer-Reviewed Study

- The main source is a scientific article titled *“Fish biomass and functional diversity recovery following a fishing ban in Luoma Lake of the Huai River Basin, China,”* published on **20 July 2026** in the journal *Ecological Processes*. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13717-026-00726-0?utm_source=openai))
  
- Study design:
  - Data collected over **six years (2018–2023)**, broken into **three years before** the fishing ban (2018–2020) and **three years after** (2021–2023). ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13717-026-00726-0?utm_source=openai))
  - Ban fully enacted on **10 May 2021**, eliminating all fishing pressure in Luoma Lake. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13717-026-00726-0?utm_source=openai))
  
### Key Findings

1. **Fish Biomass**
   - Fish biomass per sampling site rose from about **1,003 ± 685 grams** before the ban to **2,146 ± 1,558 grams** after. This is a **statistically significant increase**, p < 0.01. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13717-026-00726-0?utm_source=openai))

2. **Abundance & Species Richness**
   - Number of individuals (abundance) did **not** change significantly. Before: ~107 individuals/site; After: ~96 individuals/site; p = 0.47. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13717-026-00726-0?utm_source=openai))
   - Species richness and traditional measures of taxonomic diversity (e.g. Shannon, Simpson) also showed no significant change. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13717-026-00726-0?utm_source=openai))

3. **Functional Diversity & Community Composition**
   - **Functional richness** (FRic) increased significantly after the ban; other functional diversity metrics like evenness and dispersion remained more stable. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13717-026-00726-0?utm_source=openai))
   - Community composition shifted measurably. Certain species declined sharply (e.g. *Pseudorasbora parva*), others increased. The biomass of *Cyprinus carpio* and *Pseudobrama simoni* increased significantly; *P. parva* declined. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13717-026-00726-0?utm_source=openai))
   - Traits like age at first maturity, mouth position, feeding habit, body shape, and life-history strategy showed trait–environment associations consistent with ecological recovery. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13717-026-00726-0?utm_source=openai))

---

### Independent Reporting

- **Times of India**: Summarized the findings, stating that six years after the ban, **fish biomass has doubled**, and the lake supports a wider variety of species. ([timesofindia.indiatimes.com](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/science/chinas-luoma-lake-lost-fishing-pressure-in-2021-six-years-later-fish-biomass-has-doubled-and-the-lake-is-supporting-a-wider-variety-of-species-/amp_articleshow/132579594.cms?utm_source=openai))

- The independent reporting appears to draw directly from the scientific article, without adding new measured data beyond what the study presents. The language (“six years later”, “biomass has doubled”, “wider variety”) matches the results (biomass up ~2x; more species recorded). ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13717-026-00726-0?utm_source=openai))

---

## Completed / Measured Outcome Versus Plans or Claims

- This is a **measured outcome**, not just a pledge or announcement. The study presents empirical data before and after the ban, with statistical tests confirming significant changes. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13717-026-00726-0?utm_source=openai))

- There is **no indication** that these results are projections or models—they are based on observed, field-collected data over six years. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13717-026-00726-0?utm_source=openai))

---

## Limitations & Context to Keep in Mind

- **Time frame**: Recovery is still described as **early or transitional**; not all functional diversity metrics have fully recovered (e.g. functional evenness, dispersion remain stable). ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13717-026-00726-0?utm_source=openai))

- **Alpha diversity** (species richness, Shannon, Simpson indices) did **not** increase significantly. So while biomass and functional richness improved, overall species richness/evenness did not (within that time frame). ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13717-026-00726-0?utm_source=openai))

- **Dominance of opportunistic species**: After ban, opportunistic strategists (species with fast life histories) made up ~93.6% of total abundance, indicating ecosystem still shifting. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13717-026-00726-0?utm_source=openai))

---

## Summary Note

- The fishing ban in **Luoma Lake, China**, enacted on **10 May 2021**, has led to a **significant increase in fish biomass** (about double per site) during the three years after the ban compared to the three years before. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13717-026-00726-0?utm_source=openai))

- The lake’s **functional richness** also increased significantly, and the composition of fish species shifted, reflecting recovery of some traits and larger-bodied species. However, total abundance and taxonomic diversity (species richness, evenness) did **not** show significant change in that same period. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13717-026-00726-0?utm_source=openai))

- Independent sources confirm these results and report that the lake now supports a wider variety of species. ([timesofindia.indiatimes.com](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/science/chinas-luoma-lake-lost-fishing-pressure-in-2021-six-years-later-fish-biomass-has-doubled-and-the-lake-is-supporting-a-wider-variety-of-species-/amp_articleshow/132579594.cms?utm_source=openai))
